sentence: Naproxen is a painkiller that also treats inflammation, and it belongs to the group of medicines called NSAIDs.

It can also help with joint and muscle pain, gout, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, sprains and strains.

sentence: The NHS lists constipation or diarrhoea, dizziness, feeling sleepy or tired, bloating and stomach pain, headaches, feeling or being sick, a rash and ringing in the ears as common side effects.

Vomiting blood or dark particles that look like coffee grounds, blood in the poo or black poo that looks like tar can be signs of bleeding in the stomach or gut.

sentence: The NHS says people can drink alcohol while taking naproxen, but limiting it is advised because alcohol can increase the risk of stomach ulcers or bleeding.
In pregnancy, naproxen is not usually recommended because it may affect the baby, in particular their circulation and the level of amniotic fluid.
Doctors will only advise it if the benefits clearly outweigh the risks.
Naproxen passes into breast milk in small amounts and is unlikely to harm a baby, though there have been one or two reports of side effects in babies.
Large amounts or long use of anti-inflammatories like naproxen can affect ovulation, which may make it harder to get pregnant.
Both are NSAIDs, a group of painkillers that also reduce inflammation.
